result:
I've written the answers to `answer.json`. I checked the customer counts (b, f) and the number of orders a second way with SQL, and both gave the same results (247, 233 and 1,262 orders). Segment net sales and category net sales add up to the same total, so those two match as well.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest Q3 net sales | consumer, 299,447,269 KRW |
| b. Customers with a paid order in Q3 | 247 |
| c. Category with the highest Q3 net sales | sw, 307,901,608 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-07 (298,599,726 KRW) |
| e. Customer with the largest Q3 refund total | u161@ex.com (3,357,100 KRW) |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders in Q3 | 233 |
| g. Average net sales per Q3 paid order | 675,035 KRW (1,262 orders) |
| h. September growth over August | -9.4% (August 290,256,850 → September 263,037,636) |

**Data notes and one judgment call:**
- The 300 customer accounts belong to 250 unique emails. I counted customers by email for b, e and f.
- Some people with the same email have different segments on different accounts. For a, I used the segment of the account that placed each order, not one segment per person. Picking one segment per email would change the result for a.
- Segment values had stray spaces and mixed case (e.g. `' consumer'`, `'Enterprise '`, `'SMB'`), and I normalized them.
- Order statuses are paid, pending and cancelled, and I counted only paid. All timestamps share one UTC format, and I converted them to Korean time (+9 hours) before assigning dates.
- No refund was larger than the quantity on its order line, and none pointed to a missing order line.

STATUS: DONE
